memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Support: while comparing room types for the Boston family stay, Marcus explicitly prioritized the available balcony room but treated the balcony as a soft preference, accepting the first-floor Cambridge suite without one and declining to eliminate an otherwise stronger hotel.

messages.content: Pull the two Boston hotels back up for October 9 through 13. I want the actual sleeping setup for all three of us, the complete four-night prices, and how much time each location adds to the museum and waterfront plans. Don’t reserve anything.

The two finalists are the Harborline Back Bay and the Kendall House Cambridge. Harborline’s quoted room is a Balcony Two Doubles: two standard double beds, maximum occupancy four. The four nightly rates total $1,186; the $35 nightly destination fee adds $140, and taxes add $218.18, for $1,544.18 complete. Breakfast is not included. Kendall House is a one-bedroom suite with one king bed in the bedroom and a full-size sofa bed in the living room. Its nightly rates total $1,286, taxes are $188.42, and there is no destination fee, making the complete total $1,474.42. The package includes breakfast for three each morning.
Are those prices definitely based on three guests, not the default two-adult search? Owen is 12.

Yes. I re-ran both for two adults and one 12-year-old. Harborline permits up to four people in the two-double room and does not add a third-guest charge. Kendall House permits four in the suite, and its quoted rate covers all three occupants. Breakfast is also listed for three registered guests, not merely two adults.
The sofa bed wording is the part I don’t trust. Does the Cambridge hotel actually prepare it, or are we assuming there’s bedding somewhere in the room?

Kendall House confirmed that the sofa opens to a full-size bed. Housekeeping can make it before arrival with sheets, pillows, and a blanket at no charge. The request must be attached to the reservation, but it is not guaranteed merely by selecting three guests online. A rollaway cannot be added to that suite. Harborline’s two beds are both conventional doubles and require no preparation request.
Good. Compare the travel times. Use the Museum of Fine Arts for Friday and Long Wharf for the waterfront day.

From Harborline Back Bay, allow about 12-18 minutes to the Museum of Fine Arts by Green Line or roughly 25 minutes walking. Long Wharf is about 18-25 minutes by transit or 15-25 minutes by car, depending on traffic. From Kendall House, the museum is about 28-35 minutes by transit or 20-30 minutes by car. Long Wharf is about 25-35 minutes by transit or 15-25 minutes by car. Harborline is therefore the more convenient base for both planned outings, especially the museum.
And the nearest transit stops plus Logan. I don’t need every possible route, just the practical one from each hotel.

Harborline is about a 5-minute walk from Copley station and 7 minutes from Back Bay station. From Logan, estimate 20-35 minutes by car Thursday evening or 35-50 minutes using the airport shuttle and subway. Kendall House is about a 7-minute walk from Kendall/MIT station. From Logan, estimate 15-30 minutes by car or 35-45 minutes by Silver Line and Red Line. For Monday’s airport trip, allow 35 minutes by car from either property plus a traffic cushion; transit is approximately 45-55 minutes from Harborline and 40-50 minutes from Kendall House.
What does that translate to over the trip, not just one direction at a time?

Using transit for the Friday museum round trip and the waterfront round trip, Harborline comes to roughly 60-86 minutes total in transit. Kendall House comes to roughly 106-140 minutes. Harborline saves about 46-54 minutes across those two days. Airport transit partly offsets that by around 5 minutes each way in Kendall House’s favor, so Harborline still saves approximately 35-45 minutes over the full stay if you use transit throughout.
The Back Bay room’s balcony is a real room feature, correct? Not just a request?

Correct. The quoted category is specifically Balcony Two Doubles, and the balcony is guaranteed when that room type is confirmed. It is a small furnished balcony rather than a shared terrace. Kendall House’s one-bedroom suite does not have a balcony; the currently available suite is on the first floor.

Keep the balcony room ahead when one is available for this kind of family trip. That said, it’s a preference, not a reason to throw out a better hotel. A first-floor room like the Cambridge suite is fine without one.

Understood. I’ll give Harborline credit for the guaranteed private balcony, while keeping Kendall House fully in consideration because the first-floor suite still works and offers materially more space.
Put some value on breakfast so the totals are comparable, but don’t pretend we would eat a full hotel breakfast every morning.

Using a conservative $35 per morning for three people on only three of the four mornings, breakfast adds $105 to Harborline. That makes its practical lodging-and-breakfast comparison $1,649.18 versus $1,474.42 at Kendall House, where breakfast for three is included all four mornings. Kendall House is $174.76 lower on that basis. Without assigning any value to breakfast, it is $69.76 lower.
What are the refund cutoffs, and which one would you narrow this to right now?

Harborline is refundable through 6:00 p.m. local time on Monday, October 6; after that, the penalty is the full stay. Kendall House is refundable through 11:59 p.m. local time on Sunday, October 5; after that, the first night plus tax is charged. I would narrow to Kendall House: it is $69.76 less before meals, includes breakfast for three, gives Marcus and Daniel a separate bedroom, and the sofa bed can be prepared for Owen. Harborline has the better refund deadline, a guaranteed balcony, ordinary beds for everyone, and saves about 35-45 minutes over the trip, so it remains a credible alternate rather than an elimination.

Narrow it to Kendall House, then. The separate room and prepared sofa bed outweigh the extra travel, and breakfast makes the price gap meaningful. Keep every Harborline figure in the record in case the Cambridge rate changes. No reservation yet.

Selected without booking: Kendall House Cambridge one-bedroom suite for Thursday, October 9 through Monday, October 13. The king bedroom and full sofa bed accommodate three; the rate covers all three guests, and the no-charge sofa-bed preparation must be requested when booking. Four nights total $1,474.42 including taxes, with no destination fee and breakfast for three included. Cancel by 11:59 p.m. Sunday, October 5. It is about 7 minutes from Kendall/MIT, 28-35 minutes by transit to the Museum of Fine Arts, 25-35 minutes to Long Wharf, 15-30 minutes by car or 35-45 minutes by transit from Logan, and about 40-50 minutes by transit to Logan Monday. Harborline Back Bay remains the alternate at $1,544.18 complete: Balcony Two Doubles for up to four guests, $1,186 in room charges, $140 in destination fees, and $218.18 in taxes. Breakfast is excluded; adding a conservative $105 makes its comparison total $1,649.18. It is refundable through 6:00 p.m. October 6, about 5 minutes from Copley and 7 minutes from Back Bay station, 12-18 minutes by transit to the museum, 18-25 minutes to Long Wharf, 20-35 minutes by car or 35-50 minutes by transit from Logan, and 45-55 minutes by transit to Logan Monday. Nothing has been reserved.
